quest.title: Dream of Farewell
quest.description: The artificial dream failed to erase suffering but instead created a sweet illusion. It has gone out of control and eventually collapsed. Everyone has now returned to reality with mixed feelings...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x425, Primogem x60, Mora x27825, Guide to Ingenuity x5, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Inform A Moment of Dreams' participants of the situation

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: Oh, great. You're awake!

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: Everybody has started to wake up, and we've heard similar reports from around the city as well.

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: From the looks of it, you were able to successfully resolve the issue!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes, although it took us a good deal of effort.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: There will be many people gathering here shortly, so please do your best to maintain order.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I need to go to the Akademiya with them now, but we'll be back soon.

talks.objective: Deliver the knowledge capsule containing Moseis' consciousness to the Akademiya

dialogues.speaker: Sitt
dialogues.text: Oh, it's the great Dendro Archon. How can I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I would like to check the registration records of a Kshahrewar scholar. He should be in an unconscious state right now.

dialogues.speaker: Sitt
dialogues.text: Okay, just a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a while...

dialogues.speaker: Sitt
dialogues.text: Sorry to keep you waiting, Dendro Archon. We have confirmed that there's a scholar named Beynuni who's been unconscious for a while. The cause was improper operation of the Akasha.

dialogues.speaker: Sitt
dialogues.text: He hasn't regained consciousness yet, and is still receiving treatment at Bimarstan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Isn't his name Moseis?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I guess he didn't want to be recognized or bothered by anyone.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Please give the knowledge stored in this to the matra, and ask them to import it into Beynuni's brain.

dialogues.speaker: Sitt
dialogues.text: Understood, but for safety reasons, I need to know why.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's simple: This contains his consciousness. It's long been trapped inside of a dream.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: He's committed an act that affected the safety of Sumeru. After he wakes up, I'll inform the General Mahamatra of all the details.

dialogues.speaker: Sitt
dialogues.text: I see. I'll take care of this right away. Thank you, great Dendro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. No problem.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Alright, everyone should have gathered at "A Moment of Dreams" by now. Let's head back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's be quiet and just listen in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: I wonder what she's going to say.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hello, all of you who have just woken up.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm sorry for interrupting your beautiful dreams. I may have acted a little cold when handling things in the dream. I sincerely apologize for that.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Dreams have amazing power. They inspire us to remain resolute in the face of adversity, and help those with aspirations achieve their desires.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But dreams also have the potential to exploit people, confuse the senses, and distort the truth. Unfortunately, you were all chosen as prey for an elaborate scheme.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: As I've said before, I'm still learning, and cannot fully empathize with the pain of all the loss you've experienced.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But just take a good look around you, and you'll see many other people who have had similar experiences.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You should be proud that you've been able to gather here and look toward the future together.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The path of life is long, and it's hard for us to see the destination. This leads us to ask a lot of difficult questions...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: What's the meaning of life? What's the purpose of my existence? Why do I keep experiencing pain and loss?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: *sigh* Of course, the most comfortable choice is to stop progressing, give up thinking, and just keep repeating whatever you're already familiar with.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Whenever you have such thoughts, just look at the people and things around you.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Some people work hard all day so that their families can have a hot meal on the table at night.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Some people travel all over the world in order to create art that resonates with all of Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Some venture in search of the world's secrets to prevent rapidly approaching, yet still unknown, world-shattering catastrophes.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Life is not just about yourself. Each and every one of your actions shapes you and the world around you.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: *sigh* Look, friends and family will remember what you've done, and even some people you've never met may benefit from your actions.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Therefore, many people will strive forward to forge new paths, even if they have to endure great pain to do so.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Once you begin your journey on that same difficult yet rewarding path, you'll come to know the answers to those big, existential questions, yet they will no longer feel as life-defining as they did before.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But if you were to believe that life is nothing but an empty, ephemeral dream, then that's also the only thing it'll ever become.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You are free to choose how you want to live your lives, but as your archon, I should first make this information known to everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: In the end, it's up to you whether you want to embrace a beautiful dream at the cost of your real life.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're amazing, Nahida! Even Paimon was nearly won over by that scholar in that dream.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Well, he's very good at manipulating the weaknesses of human nature, but perhaps he himself had fallen prisoner to them long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That dream was incredibly beautiful and enticing. Ordinary people couldn't see through it, and easily lost themselves within it.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But as long as you can still wake up, you can still move forward with your life.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You've also learned a lot, Nahida.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Huh? What makes you say that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You can really empathize with others now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! You said that you didn't understand human feelings, but we saw how considerate you were with all these people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your speech just now really connected with everyone. You did a good job!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Thank you. I've heard a lot of sad stories along this journey, and several of them have touched my heart.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You can't say that the victims of the dream really did anything wrong, and what they wanted was also not unreasonable...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That's why I could understand them when they tried to resist us and protect the dream.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But all of my understanding and stirred feelings probably can't even account for even one percent of the pain they've experienced.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I don't think this "one percent" can be seen as an example of what you call empathy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're too hard on yourself that's for sure.

choices.text: Nobody is capable of having absolute empathy.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hehe, alright. I suppose going out into the world will help my confidence grow.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I've learned that emotions are nothing like knowledge, and that's why it's hard for me to put them into words sometimes.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Beynuni, or "Moseis," said that I had never personally felt the pain of loss, but I have a vague feeling that this isn't true.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The moment I entered the dream, I felt like I was wrapped in a blanket of warm feelings.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It was so warm that it felt like I had returned to the start of my life, and I didn't want to wake up anymore.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Huh... Did she see something in the dream, too?)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But when I opened my eyes, the feeling was gone without a trace.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If I have to make an analogy for it, I would say I can no longer see words on a piece of paper after they have been erased, but I can still see the slight indentations of where the words had been written.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But now that I've experienced this dream... I think I can say with confidence that I won't dwell too much on the meaning of that warmth.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's enough that I can tell I was once supported by that warmth, and its existence has allowed me to get to where I am today.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If I dwell too much on its exact nature, I would be putting the cart before the horse.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I gave a speech to inspire my people, so if I were to fail to live up to those words myself, then that would be too embarrassing, hehe.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Greater Lord Rukkhadevata has already shaped Nahida through her actions.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Even if she has been forgotten, Nahida's mind and willpower are the proof that she once existed.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Instead of telling her the truth, I should respect their decisions.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, what's with that serious look?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You keep looking like there's something you want to say. Is there anything you want to tell me?

choices.text: Uh, I forgot what I wanted to say.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hehe, okay.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Since we just woke up, let's stretch a little bit.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: A new day is about to begin.

choices.text: You should be a little more confident in yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Thank you for rescuing me. I'm really sorry. Luckily, Haydar wasn't injured because of my stupid mistake...

dialogues.speaker: Haydar
dialogues.text: Dad said you're amazing. You're real heroes, thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Kathya
dialogues.text: I'm getting ready to go on an adventure, and I'm taking this plant with me.

dialogues.speaker: Kathya
dialogues.text: I shouldn't just sit here waiting for her to come back. Professor Aisha was so determined to explore those secrets, so I should go take a look, too.

dialogues.speaker: Kathya
dialogues.text: Thank you. May we meet again in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: I discovered that Nasser and I get along pretty well. We both have pretty straightforward personalities.

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: It also turns out we both disagreed with the Dendro Archon. One in real life and one in the dream, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Kian
dialogues.text: I'm still a little dizzy from sleeping so long... Just give me a moment here...

dialogues.speaker: Inas
dialogues.text: Since we were neighbors in the dream, how about we rent a place together?

dialogues.speaker: Thana
dialogues.text: Sounds good. I can't afford a house on my own anyway... But I'm sure life will get better.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: I felt a violent tremor somewhere deep within my dream, and then I woke up.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: I guess we'll all wake up from our dreams sooner or later...

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: They all started waking up around the same time. That's pretty amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Sitt
dialogues.text: I'll take care of it as soon as possible. Don't worry.

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: I'm really glad I reached out to you earlier. Otherwise, we wouldn't have been able to handle this situation on our own.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You did a great job as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are we going to ask about that scholar?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes, but it may take some time for him to wake up after his consciousness returns to his body.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We can leave the rest to the matra.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: (The Traveler and the Dendro Archon must have done something deep inside the dream.)

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: (That's our Dendro Archon. I have to say, I'm very impressed.)

dialogues.speaker: Sitt
dialogues.text: (I've gotta be careful not to slip up with my work, especially in front of someone as important as the Dendro Archon.)

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: (Finally, it's over... It all went perfectly, but it was way too tiring, ugh...)

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: (I'm so lucky Haydar wasn't hurt...)

dialogues.speaker: Haydar
dialogues.text: (Dad is the best!)

dialogues.speaker: Kathya
dialogues.text: (All this time, I never realized that this is what Professor Aisha wanted... How did I not see it earlier?)

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: (Should we celebrate and go eat something special?)

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: (I should buy her a drink later.)

dialogues.speaker: Kian
dialogues.text: (So dizzy... I think I'm about to lose my lunch.)

dialogues.speaker: Inas
dialogues.text: (I guess it'll take some time for me to get used to my new life, but that's fine with me.)

dialogues.speaker: Thana
dialogues.text: (I'm so happy I've finally found a place to stay.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida said she wanted to speak with us alone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems like she went to the plaza in front of the Akademiya.
